html:
The Yurí, or Jurí, were a people of the forests between the Caquetá (Japurá) and Putumayo rivers, on today's border of Colombia and Brazil. Their language is thought to be related to that of the Ticuna.

Portuguese slave raiders and traders took many Yurí from the 1700s, and by the 1800s they had disappeared from the records. Some researchers think an uncontacted group living today near the Puré River in Colombia may descend from them. Neighbours included the Bora and Huitoto.
